A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BGDA/AdaptiveBGDA study. The main text, four tables, three figures, and Appendices A–F are available and can be reliably matched despite changes in pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original PINN training results across 22 PDE tasks, gradient-balance measurements, and additional optimizer and architecture experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix A, including the benchmark comparisons and optimizer ablation.

M1.justification: The regularized saddle-point objective, BGDA and AdaptiveBGDA algorithms, and stochastic S-BGDA procedure in Appendix F are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 22 PINNacle PDE tasks, including complex geometry, multiple domains, varying coefficients, long-time, chaotic, high-dimensional, and inverse problems.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Adam, LBFGS, LRA, NTK, RAR, and MultiAdam. Appendix A retains the same Adam+Adam and RMSProp+RMSProp comparisons against Adam+RMSProp.

E3.justification: Both retain L2RE, the three 10,000-epoch windows in Section 6.1, and training to the performance limit in the benchmark tables. The reported learning rates, decay schedule, and adaptive parameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: The Poisson 2d-C gradient-imbalance analysis, spatial error comparison, and Appendix A optimizer-combination ablation are retained without added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same gradient-ratio means, reported variances, and three-sigma overlap argument. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–3 retain the same results. For example, AdaptiveBGDA's Poisson 2d-C L2RE remains 8.16E-3, and its reported benchmark dominance remains 72.7%.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, lemmas, convergence bounds, and proofs in Appendices B–F are mathematically unchanged. Additional equation labels and changes to lemma formatting are typographical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims about the non-Euclidean saddle-point formulation, theoretical guarantees, training stability, and benchmark superiority.

C2.justification: The explanations of gradient balancing, optimizer choice, and task-specific performance are unchanged. Both retain the discussion of unresolved general-case rate improvement and the weakness on Burgers 2d-C.

D1.justification: The hardware descriptions, hyperparameters, PINNacle implementation basis, and code-link destination are identical. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning against earlier weighting and saddle-point methods are unchanged. The reference lists match after accounting for whitespace and pagination.

P1.justification: The affiliation block removes Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology and the Institute for System Programming, RAS, and revises affiliation markers. Scientific prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes the first-page logos and lemma boxes, places the captions of Tables 1 and 3 below their tables, and reflows text and displays. Several appendix inequalities receive separate labels on their two lines; figure contents and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes affiliations and limited aspects of formatting while preserving the method, empirical evidence in Section 6 and Appendix A, proofs, and reproducibility information. These presentation adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in the paper's scientific support or overall usability.
